task.name: Stair Climbing
task.objective: Improve one reward program for the unified Stair task across runner-owned C0/C1 training regimes, with OOD performance as the primary emphasis and in-distribution performance protected by named guards.

candidate_may: replace the complete reward with pure RewardTerm callables
use only fields declared by the task reward input contract
set finite weights and optional bounded output clips
evidence_discipline: Before authoring, compare the proposed mechanism with public_history.experiment_memory, recent_outcomes, and current-best evidence.
Treat lower scores, failed gates, and dominating or negligible runtime component contributions as negative evidence; do not silently repeat or combine those mechanisms.

Treat last_mean only as the last sampled weighted-contribution snapshot; never infer that a component is inactive or causally ineffective from last_mean alone. Compare max_abs, repeated runtime evidence, and fixed evaluation outcomes.

If reusing a rejected mechanism, the canonical hypothesis narrative embedded in TrainingComponents.rationale must name the closest prior candidate, state the exact code-level difference, and explain how it addresses the observed failure; keep mechanical repair notes out of that hypothesis.
Do not submit numeric-only, string-only, or formatting-only variants of an evaluated source; the historical-source gate rejects those variants before training.
Prefer the accepted current-best source, or when none exists the explicitly nonaccepted best-observed bootstrap anchor.

When an authoring anchor is present, change exactly one named canonical prompt-visible component mechanism relative to it and preserve every other component mechanism; without an anchor, author the complete initial component set.

reward_integration.candidate_usage: Return raw reward rates; the dispatcher applies weight, clip and dt once.

high_risk_axis_semantics.environment: dim0=independent environments at one control step; output[i] only from input[i]; no diff/roll/cumsum/sort/index/reduction across dim0; declared history fields carry time
high_risk_axis_semantics.support_contact_force_history: axes=[env,history(0 newest; larger older),support(opaque members),xyz]; contact=norm xyz,max all 3 history,then threshold; this window alone does not identify every onset within a control step
high_risk_axis_semantics.spatial_vectors: components=[x,y,z]; world +x stair-forward,+y left,+z up; body/yaw +x robot-forward,+y left,+z up

remaining_goal_distance_m.sign: positive before, zero at, negative beyond goal

base_height.reference_frame: terrain origin at the bottom start platform
base_height.candidate_usage: Includes staircase elevation, not clearance above the supporting step; standing-height thresholds do not prove posture or support. Use roll/pitch/projected_gravity, goal_progress_fraction, and contact fields.

projected_gravity.reference_frame: FLU base frame (+x forward,+y left,+z up)
projected_gravity.candidate_usage: Use -z for upright reward; +z favors inversion.

height_scan.sensor_semantics: downward terrain scan; positive=lower/farther, negative=higher/closer; no overhead or torso obstacle sensing
height_scan.candidate_usage: Use order-invariant reductions only; ray directions are not exposed.

raw_physical_magnitudes.candidate_usage: New or modified RewardTerms using these fields require finite clip_min and clip_max. Callable-only transforms do not replace this final clip; runtime clips before weight. Exact unchanged reference mechanisms are exempt only by canonical structure signature. The declared clip and weight expose the resulting weighted bound.

forbidden_contact_force.semantics: current resolved forbidden-contact role force vectors in Newtons
forbidden_contact_force.candidate_usage: Use forbidden_contact for the task-owned binary failure signal; dense force terms follow raw_physical_magnitudes.

termination_masks.candidate_usage: Frozen Stair: forbidden_contact and terminated_non_timeout are identical masks; do not add both.

progress_fraction.semantics: elapsed fraction of the current episode horizon
progress_fraction.candidate_usage: For episode-time scheduling only; it does not mean training progress, position, proximity to the top, or completion. Spatial progress is goal_progress_fraction.

goal_progress_fraction.semantics: instantaneous clamped spatial position from the frozen start coordinate toward the frozen goal coordinate
goal_progress_fraction.temporal_behavior: recomputed every control step; may decrease when the robot moves backward; not latched, absorbing, or a completion event

support_contact_force.semantics: support/contact force in Newtons; nonzero is required for support
support_contact_force.candidate_usage: Contact is not inherently bad; normalize force-derived terms.

support_contact.semantics: boolean contact threshold over the maximum force in the configured 3-sample support_contact_force_history window

support_first_contact.semantics: contact onset observed within the last control period; not contact occupancy
support_first_contact.candidate_usage: Use this event mask with support_last_air_time for landing rewards; history-any-contact is not onset.

support_contact_time.semantics: duration of current contact episode; zero while airborne

support_air_time.semantics: duration of current airborne episode; zero in contact

support_last_air_time.semantics: duration of the last completed airborne episode, held until the next landing

opaque_axis_contract.usage_rule: Member mapping is hidden. Only whole-axis order-invariant reductions are valid; fixed or partial indexing, positional selection, and pre-reduction reshaping are forbidden. Helpers that consume these fields must be top-level functions.

joint_ood.meaning: simultaneous scalar extrapolation of stair riser height and stair tread depth

public_eval_contract.c2_evidence_scope: current evaluation-only surface/contact mechanism shift; zero training exposure; height-scan policy salience not claimed

factor_diagnostic_table.interpretation: groups overlap and are not objective weights; saturated groups remain visible as capabilities to preserve

public_eval_contract.diagnostic_interpretation: latched or recent-history correlates for hypothesis formation; they may coexist with success and do not prove failure causality

RewardTerm.training_effect: all weighted RewardTerm outputs replace the complete training reward

selection_guidance: Use only validated public failure/diagnostic/progress summaries.
After rejection, use current_best as the default parent; reuse a rejected mechanism or weight only with public evidence.
Keep each candidate attributable: change one reward mechanism, preserve current-best coefficients, and avoid unrelated retuning.

Prefer a recent-untried mechanism only when task score, failure, or progress evidence supports it. Diagnostic rates, even extreme ones, are correlates rather than optimization targets or causal proof; judge a hypothesis by objective and guard movement.
Code plus verifier/runtime evidence are authoritative over prose rationale; claim a maximum weighted contribution only with conditions, clips, weight, and an analytic bound.
Success is the first physically valid top-platform arrival; post-arrival stopping position and settling are not evaluated.
climb_completion_summary.success_rate and first_valid_top_arrival_rate describe the same absorbing task completion event.
Optimize J_primary=(2*J_OOD+J_ID)/3 while all three runner-owned named guards J_OOD, C0-ID, and C1-ID remain within their paired non-regression tolerances; no score can compensate for a failed guard.
Match candidate feedback to source_catalog by candidate_id and program_source_checksum when that source is available; reference_anchor feedback belongs to the current_best source.
When the shared candidate_capabilities section marks complete_reward_program prompt-visible, return a complete replacement reward program, not an additive patch.
Use only fields declared by the StairRewardInputsVNext contract.
Do not change training budget, PPO, seeds, terrain bins, termination rules, or acceptance rules.

Task provided examples are exposed through known_good_examples when available.
Use the latest nonaccepted source with its verifier, runtime, and eval feedback to repair, refute, or replace the attempted mechanism.
